pocSpotCheck: Classifier re-ran work/test/audit23/BonfireCapFrontRun.t.sol --match-test CODE001: test_CODE001_frontRunBurn_defeatsCap PASS, test_CODE001_capLandsFirst_payoutCapped PASS (reproduced, not taken on agent report).
classifierCorrections: DEDUP-004 overstates the loss of a safe cap sequence. setRatePerDay(0) is a one-tx owner-only stop: it checkpoints the pot (preserved), and burn() then reverts NFTBonfire__BurningDisabled (L98). The owner can then setMaxPayout(cap) with no burn able to front-run it, and re-enable the rate. The owner can also setPauser(self) and pause() (two txs; atomic if the owner is a Safe batching them). Both safe sequences exist without the global Pauser; only the pot standing when the first tx lands can escape, exactly as with pause-first.

classifiedFinding.faithfulnessCrossRef: F-01-053 stays in spec-conformance.md as a cross-reference to this L entry only. Do not file it as a second finding.
classifiedFinding.borderlineNote: Low vs Medium. Medium would need a value leak beyond what the owner set up, and there isn't one. Total AM issued is at most ratePerDay x elapsed time (invariant_1_emissionTimeBounded holds over about 1.09M forge and Medusa calls). The hazard concentrates emission the owner already budgeted into one burner's hands. It does not enlarge that emission. Would re-rate to Medium if a deploy story ships rate>0 with maxPayout==0 and no pauser, and the expected pause or wiring delay times rate exceeds a material threshold. Flag for human review.

classification.assetImpact: Antimatter (redeemable into unbacked phUSD at about $0.89/AM) that the owner meant to forfeit through a cap is minted to the first burner. This is real phUSD dilution (ECON-005), not opportunity cost. The excess is capped at (ratePerDay x D - intended cap), and that sum sits inside the owner's own rate budget.
attackPath: 1. Owner runs ratePerDay > 0 with maxPayout at its default of 0 (unlimited).
2a. Burns stop for D days: a pause (accrual continues by design), or rate enabled before setAuthorizedBurner/setApprovedMinter lands. The pot grows to rate x D.
3a. Owner unpauses, or completes the wiring, without a cap. A searcher holding any V2 NFT back-runs it with burn(id, pot-1) and takes the whole pot.
2b. Variant: the owner broadcasts setMaxPayout(cap) while burns are live. A holder front-runs it with burn() and takes the uncapped pot (PoC: 250e18 instead of 10e18).
classification.likelihood: medium-low: needs an owner config sequence (uncapped default plus an idle stretch, or reactive capping while live). That sequence is plausible because the default is uncapped and the deploy story that would require a cap does not exist. Once the setup exists, exploitation is trivial and permissionless.
classification.assumptions: rate>0; maxPayout==0 at the moment burns resume, or the cap is set while live; the attacker holds one V2 NFT (about 772 idle ones exist).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner-side configuration sequence. No user principal at risk.

classifiedFinding.justification: This is a non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3). A competent owner would not expect a reactive cap to be front-runnable, or an unpause to hand out the whole pause-period accrual. So it is in scope and is not dismissed as centralization. It rates at the impact it unlocks: the distribution of an already-budgeted emission goes wrong, and nothing extra is drained. That is Low under C4. Safe-config guidance for the phStaging2 NFTBonfire deploy story: (1) set maxPayout before or in the same tx batch as the first setRatePerDay>0; (2) never change the cap while burns are live. Stop burns first with pause() or setRatePerDay(0), then setMaxPayout, then resume; (3) set a cap before any planned pause or wiring delay.
classifiedFinding.routing: ledger L (ycn); safe-config text owed to the missing phStaging2 NFTBonfire deploy story.

classification.assetImpact: None beyond redistribution of a fixed, owner-set stream between NFT holders. A front-run honest burner keeps the NFT, because the minPayout check reverts before nftMinter.burn (L101), and loses gas only.
attackPath: n/a: copying or back-running a pending burn redirects the pot but cannot raise total emission
classification.assumptions: The user supplies a sane minPayout. minPayout=0 is a documented opt-out (C4 user-input mistake).

classifiedFinding.justification: Story-053 explicitly accepts that the pot is 'trivially front-runnable' and supplies minPayout as the remedy (Law 2 satisfied; the code matches). The mechanical PATTERN-001 'potential-medium' label is overruled: no protocol or user asset is lost. QA, plus a UI obligation (default a non-zero minPayout) for the phlimbo-ui follow-up.

classification.assetImpact: Protocol revenue goes to the wrong place, and bonfire burn tickets get cheaper. It is not a value leak out of the protocol. The payer still pays real assets to protocol-owned V1 dispatchers, so the payment moves to the wrong destination and is not stolen or lost. Bonfire emission is time-bounded and does not depend on ticket cost, so the protocol cannot be made to pay out more AM. The actual effects: (1) mint revenue that should reach the V2 dispatchers (Uniboost/UniPoolerV2) goes to the V1 dispatchers, and the gap is the difference in amount and destination between a V1 mint at about $3.6 and a V2 mint at about $10; (2) V2 price growth is bypassed; (3) an unmonitored mint path into a token that is now value-bearing.
attackPath: 1. Mint V1 idx2 for about 1.08 SCX (about $3.68), or idx1 for about 288 EYE (about $3.56).
2. NFTMigrator(0x22c0fc1a).migrate() -> NFTMinterV2.mintFor yields a V2 NFT of the same index (fork-verified at block 26280445).
3. Burn it at NFTBonfire for the pot. Price escalates 10% per mint per index.
classification.likelihood: low: profitable only if the pot is above about $3.6 and the attacker beats the holders of about 772 idle V2 NFTs. Never profitable with maxPayout below about 4 AM.
classification.assumptions: NFTBonfire is wired on mainnet; the V1 minter stays unpaused; the migrator stays authorized.
classification.externalRequirements: Live deployment state as of block 26280445.

classifiedFinding.justification: This is a non-obvious deployment-state footgun (Law 3). The owner retired NFTMigrator from mainnet-addresses.ts in phStaging2 story-059, and would be surprised that a retired migrator now mints redeemable bonfire tickets. Story-053 (ycn) is what turned an inert authorization into a value-bearing one. Low, not Medium: no emission beyond budget, no user loss, and the redirected revenue is small and bounded by escalating V1 prices. Scope: it belongs in the ycn ledger. The in-scope ycn change (NFTBonfire making every NFTMinterV2 token redeemable) is what activates it, and the authorization being exploited is NFTMinterV2.authorizedMinters, a ycn contract's state. Under Law 1 a finding is not dropped because its fix sits in another repo. The fix (setAuthorizedMinter(0x22c0..., false) and/or pause V1 0xd936461f, then confirm there are no other authorized minters) is routed to the phStaging2 NFTBonfire deploy story. Same handling as L-27: a later ycn rescan that still sees it is not an incomplete fix until the phStaging2 story lands.
classifiedFinding.routing: ledger L (ycn), fix routed to phStaging2.

classifiedFinding.borderlineNote: QA vs Low. Classed QA because the premise that the pause-first cap sequence is unavailable is wrong (see classifierCorrections): setRatePerDay(0) is a one-tx owner stop that blocks burns and keeps the pot, and setPauser(self)+pause() is also open to the owner. What remains is a documented operational gap: the global Pauser does not reach the bonfire until setPauser + Pauser.register land, and story-053 L102/L21/L128 already state this and assign it to the phStaging2 follow-up. Re-rate to Low if the phStaging2 deploy story omits Pauser registration.

classification.assetImpact: None directly. During an incident, the global Pauser does not stop bonfire burns or AM mints until it is wired. The owner keeps an immediate stop (setRatePerDay(0)).
attackPath: n/a: availability or operational gap, no attacker gain beyond DEDUP-001
classification.assumptions: The owner relies on the global Pauser alone during an incident.

classifiedFinding.justification: Story-documented behaviour (Law 2 satisfied), with working owner-side stops, so there is no availability impact that rises to Low. Keep it visible as a QA operational note with safe-config guidance: the deploy story must setPauser(globalPauser) and Pauser.register(bonfire). Runbook note: setRatePerDay(0) is the one-tx stop that does not need the pauser. The NFTMinterV2.burn/mintFor pause-bypass facet (a) reconciles to existing ledger L-04 674c799b2058 and must not be re-filed.
classifiedFinding.routing: qa-report.md; facet (a) -> L-04 674c799b2058 lastSeen bump only.

classification.assetImpact: None in yield-claim-nft. Cross-project: it voids the 'NFT has no realizable redemption value' premise behind phoenix-nft-staking 858e9e80 (wont-fix) and 521c20ad (open).
classification.assumptions: The quantitative margin holds at sane rates (per MR23-001).

It must stay visible (Law 1) through manual-review.json MR23-001 and a phoenix-nft-staking triage note.
